title: Course-of-values recursion on the naturals, as a named kernel principle with its unfolding equation
statement: If a property (or a construction, at any universe) holds at n whenever it holds at every m < n, then it holds at every n -- and the resulting function satisfies the expected unfolding equation, so a proof about it can take its first step. Both are kernel terms over Nat.lt_well_founded and the generic WellFounded.fix, with an empty axiom footprint.

formal.statement: def Nat.strongInduction.{u} (motive : Nat -> Sort u) (step : forall n, (forall m, m < n -> motive m) -> motive n) (n : Nat) : motive n
formal.kernel_statement: Nat.strongInduction.{u} : forall (motive : Nat -> Sort u), (forall n, (forall m, Nat.lt m n -> motive m) -> motive n) -> forall n, motive n, defined as WellFounded.fix.{1,u} Nat Nat.lt motive Nat.lt_well_founded. Nat.strongInduction_eq.{u} : forall motive step n, Eq.{u} (motive n) (Nat.strongInduction motive step n) (step n (fun m _ => Nat.strongInduction motive step m)).

provenance.established_by: axeyum lane `hall-sufficiency`: `nat_prelude/strong_induction.rs`. ADR-1614, closing ADR-1608's item 1.
provenance.source: Course-of-values induction; standard, and derivable from the well-foundedness of < which this prelude already proved (Nat.lt_well_founded, order.rs).

prior_art.establishes: the same principle; this one is stated with an explicit motive because there is no elaborator here and every application is built positionally

evidence.supports: the recursion principle itself, at any universe
checkers: Kernel::add_declaration (re-derives the type from the proof term)
evidence.notes: The evaluation test is not decorative: a wrapper that did not reduce would type-check identically. `strongInduction (fun _ => Nat) (fun n ih => succ n) 3` must reduce to 4, which forces WellFounded.fix to reduce its accessibility proof at the numeral; 3 is named as the answer a step returning n would give.
evidence.checker_paired_negative: The evaluation test pins the value away from 3 as well as at 4, so a step that ignored its own argument in the other direction fails.

evidence.supports: the unfolding equation, without which a proof about a strongly-recursive definition cannot take its first step
checkers: Kernel::add_declaration (re-derives the type from the proof term)
evidence.notes: `strongInduction motive step n` does not reduce at a symbolic n -- `lt_well_founded n` is stuck -- so the equation is a genuine theorem here and not an iota rule.
evidence.checker_paired_negative: The same proof term offered at an equation that unfolds at `succ n` while its recursive argument still ranges below `n` must be REJECTED. That is a one-`succ` slide and the smallest one that separates the equation from a different statement.

evidence.supports: the declaration exists under this exact name, and did not before
evidence.checker_command: cargo run --release -q -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example shape_search -- --name Nat.strongInduction --kind definition --expect 1
evidence.notes: The pre-state: at declarations=2832 with positive control Nat.Rado.IsRadoNumber FOUND, `--name-like strong` returned ABSENT, confirming ADR-1608's measurement. `Nat.base_induction` is a different statement. Eight modules in this prelude (gcd, bezout, factorization, irrational, base_induction, count_range_reversal, totient_dvd_chain, totient_gcd_mul) already spelled the five-argument WellFounded.fix application by hand; none was rewritten by this lane.

notes: epistemic_status and external_status agree: this is a standard principle and the machinery it is built from (Nat.lt_well_founded plus WellFounded.fix) was already here. What was missing was the NAME, and ADR-1608 measured that absence while sizing Hall's marriage theorem. The motive is explicit rather than implicit, and the universe is Sort u rather than Prop, so the same wrapper covers course-of-values definitions and not only proofs.
